summary: For MIT work, use the approved tool and data-risk path, disclose academic or research AI use, and keep High Risk MIT information out of generative AI; check your course or exam instructions for any further rule.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed MIT student coursework permission rule is included; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
No source-backed MIT student exam-use rule is included; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
MIT advises disclosure of generative-AI use for academic, educational, and research-related uses. Scope: MIT community guidance.

do: Disclose AI use in the academic or research context covered by the guidance.
dont: Do not publish AI-assisted research without disclosing the nature of that use.

dimensions.summary: MIT states that no generative-AI tool is approved for High Risk MIT information, and public tools are not recommended for MIT research or educational activities.

do: Classify MIT information and use only the permitted risk path.
dont: Do not put High Risk MIT information into a generative-AI tool.

dimensions.summary: MIT maintains an IS&T-licensed approved-tools list for low- and medium-risk information. A listed tool is an institutional path, not permission for a particular class, exam, or research output.

do: Check the current MIT list and data-risk condition before use.
dont: Do not infer course or assessment permission from the list.

dimensions.summary: MIT guidance calls for disclosure when research results rely on AI-generated content. No broader MIT authorship rule is asserted here.

do: Describe AI involvement in research-related work where the guidance applies.
dont: Do not hide AI-generated content relied on in published research.
